## Executive Summary

> **Purpose**: This white paper makes the strategic case for how software should be *decomposed* when the builders are autonomous AI agents. It is the narrative companion to the governing decision ([ADR-GOV-011](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-011-architecture-pipeline-operating-model.md)) and the standards, patterns, and guidance that implement it.

Gainwell is adopting AI agents as first-class software builders. The value is enormous — parallel, spec-driven delivery at a pace human-only teams cannot match. But the way we have historically decomposed work — into behavioral requirements (user stories, BDD scenarios) — was designed for human teams who fill the gaps between requirements with conversation, tribal knowledge, and integration testing. **Autonomous agents do not have those gap-fillers.** An agent builds exactly what it is pointed at, in isolation, and cannot converge on an unspecified interface with another agent by talking in a hallway.

Behavioral decomposition specifies the **nodes** of a system — its observable capabilities — but is structurally blind to the **edges**: the API, event, and policy contracts that join nodes; the universal properties that must hold across all inputs; the non-functional envelope; the shared data model; the cross-context journeys; and the shared foundations that many pieces depend on. Under human delivery those edges are filled in implicitly. Under agentic delivery they are simply **not built** — each side of an interface passes its own tests against a stub, and the integration is discovered missing in production. We have observed this concretely: a user-facing layer reported "100% complete" while the service feeding it was never built, because the seam between them was in no one's backlog.

This paper argues that agentic delivery requires a **multi-axis, contract-first decomposition model**: decompose every capability along all the axes it spans (behavior, seam, negative property, non-functional, data, journey), build shared foundations before dependents fan out, and make every axis accountable through one repeatable mechanism — a design-time artifact in a recognized industry standard, an owned work item, and a merge-blocking verification gate. This is not a new methodology to learn from scratch; it reuses standards engineers already know (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, OPA/Rego, Arazzo) and treats them as the binding inputs to build rather than after-the-fact documentation.

**Key Strategic Points:**

- **Behavior-only decomposition is unsafe for autonomous agents** — the edges it omits are exactly what agents cannot infer, so they ship unbuilt.
- **A multi-axis, contract-first model makes agentic delivery safe and auditable** — every interface, property, and foundation becomes an owned, verified artifact, closing the "built by no one" failure by construction.
- **It is enforceable, not aspirational** — expressed as enterprise principles, decisions, standards, and patterns that an ARB can require and a pipeline can gate, using recognized standards to keep onboarding cost low.

### 1.1 Business Context

The economics of software delivery are shifting. AI coding agents can implement, test, and open pull requests in parallel, at a scale that makes the specification — not the coding — the bottleneck and the risk. Gainwell's move to a spec-driven, agent-executed SDLC (governed by ADR-GOV-009/010) is a deliberate bet on that shift. But a faster builder magnifies the cost of an incomplete specification: an agent will confidently build the wrong thing, or nothing, exactly where the spec is silent.

**Key Business Drivers:**

- **Agentic delivery at scale** — parallel agents make specification completeness the dominant risk, not developer throughput.
- **Regulated-healthcare accountability** — HIPAA/CMS delivery must demonstrate that security- and compliance-relevant interfaces and properties are specified and verified, not assumed.
- **Reproducibility across teams** — an enterprise accelerator must work the same way for every team, which requires a model expressed in shared standards, not one product's tribal practice.

[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#12-strategic-scope]

### 1.2 Strategic Scope

This strategy white paper focuses on:

- **How work is decomposed for agents** — the axes a capability must be broken along so that nothing an agent needs is left implicit.
- **How completeness becomes definable and enforceable** — turning "done" from a behavior-only proxy into coverage of every axis a capability spans.
- **How the model is grounded in the enterprise taxonomy** — so it is discoverable and enforceable, not trapped in a single pipeline's documentation.

[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#21-problem-statement]

### 2.1 Problem Statement

Behavioral decomposition — user stories and BDD scenarios — specifies *observable functional behavior, at a single boundary, at a point in time, for one actor, via enumerated examples*. That is a precise and useful description of a system's **nodes**. It says nothing about the **edges** and cross-cutting properties that a working system also depends on. For human teams, the omission is tolerable because humans negotiate the edges informally. For autonomous agents, the omission is the defect: the edge has no scenario, so it becomes no work item, so no agent owns it, so it is built by no one.

**What's at Stake:**

- **Silent integration failure** — features reported complete that do not work end-to-end because the seam between them was never built.
- **Unverified compliance negatives** — "PHI is never logged", "no route serves data without authorization" — assumed rather than proven, surfacing as breaches and audit findings.
- **Wasted concurrency** — parallel agents colliding on shared foundations no one declared, turning intended parallelism into rework.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#22-impact-on-the-organization]

### 2.2 Impact on the Organization

**Current State Challenges:**

- Delivery pipelines emit work from behavioral specs alone, so the majority of a distributed system's integration surface (its edges) is invisible to the work breakdown.
- Quality attributes and universal properties live as prose in design documents with no guaranteed verification.
- The one place the multi-axis model has been articulated is a single product's process guidance — non-binding, and undiscoverable to teams not already using that pipeline.

**Why Current Approaches Fall Short:**

Adding more BDD scenarios does not help — the missing things are, by definition, not example-based behaviors. Relying on integration testing to catch the gaps pushes discovery to the most expensive point and assumes the integration was attempted at all. And leaving the model as informative guidance means an ARB cannot require it and a new team will never find it. The gap is structural and must be closed structurally.

### 3.1 Strategic Framework Overview

Treat a capability as decomposing along **multiple orthogonal axes**, and make each axis accountable through one repeatable mechanism.

**Strategic Principles:**

- **Nodes *and* edges** — every cross-component edge is a first-class, owned, contracted, gated artifact, not an implicit assumption. An edge with no owner is built by no one.
- **One accountability triad per axis** — for each axis: a **design-time artifact in a recognized standard → an owned work item → a merge-blocking gate**. The same shape closes every axis, so there is one discipline to learn.
- **Foundations before fan-out** — a scaffold shared by N siblings is an explicit prerequisite built once, before the siblings fan out in parallel.
- **Recognized standards over bespoke formats** — OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, OPA/Rego, Arazzo — chosen for the human reviewer's low onboarding cost; the agent consumes whatever it is pointed at.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#component-1-the-multi-axis-decomposition-model]

#### Component 1: The multi-axis decomposition model

- **Purpose**: Ensure nothing an agent needs is left implicit by naming every axis a capability spans.
- **Business Value**: Makes "done" mean *complete across all axes*, not behavior-only — the precondition for trusting agentic output.
- **Key Capabilities**: Six axes — **behavior** (Gherkin), **seam** (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Rego), **negative property** (invariants), **NFR** (operational harnesses), **data model** (canonical shapes), **journey** (Arazzo) — each closed by the accountability triad.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#component-2-contract-first-seams-and-foundations]

#### Component 2: Contract-first seams and foundations

- **Purpose**: Turn the interfaces and shared scaffolds — the things agents cannot infer — into design-time artifacts and prerequisites.
- **Business Value**: Eliminates the "built by no one" failure and the cold-start collision; enables safe parallel/agentic delivery.
- **Key Capabilities**: Design-first seam contracts with producer/consumer accountability and served-AND-wired cohesion gates; foundation-before-fan-out sequencing; the design-vs-implementer ownership split so an agent never authors the policy that gates its own output.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#component-3-enterprise-tier-grounding]

#### Component 3: Enterprise-tier grounding

- **Purpose**: Make the model enforceable and discoverable, not trapped in one pipeline's docs.
- **Business Value**: An ARB can require it; a new team can find it; a compliance auditor can cite it.
- **Key Capabilities**: A ratified decision (ADR), guiding principles, mandatory standards per axis, reusable patterns, and authoring guidance — the taxonomy tiers that carry enforceable doctrine.
page_texts.16:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#33-expected-outcomes]

### 3.3 Expected Outcomes

**Strategic Benefits:**

- **Integration correctness by construction** — every seam is owned and gated, so end-to-end failures are caught at design/merge, not in production.
- **Auditable compliance** — negatives and authorization become verified invariants, providing HIPAA/CMS evidence.
- **Safe, real concurrency** — foundations and contracts let isolated agents converge without collision or drift.

**Success Indicators:**

- No capability reports "complete" with an unbuilt seam, an unverified compliance negative, or a declared-but-absent test harness.
- Parallel agent fan-out proceeds from a built foundation, not a cold start.
- Every axis a capability spans resolves to an enforceable standard or pattern an ARB can point to.

[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#41-strategic-roadmap]

### 4.1 Strategic Roadmap

**Implementation Philosophy:**

Ground the model top-down through the taxonomy — decision and principles first (so downstream artifacts have authority to cite), then the mandatory standards per axis, then the reusable patterns and authoring guidance — while keeping foundational, owner-governed artifacts (guiding principles, contribution process) changed only through their owners' ratification.
page_texts.20:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#phase-1-authority]

#### Phase 1: Authority

**Strategic Objectives:**

- Ratify the operating model as an enterprise decision.
- Elevate the core laws (seam accountability; multi-axis decomposition) to guiding principles.

**Key Activities:**

- Author the operating-model ADR (architecture-as-code, multi-axis, foundation-before-fan-out).
- Recommend the principle elevations to the principle owners for ARB ratification.

**Expected Outcomes:**

- A durable decision every downstream standard cites; the model discoverable from the decision tier.
page_texts.21:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#phase-2-mandate]

#### Phase 2: Mandate

**Strategic Objectives:**

- Give each requirements axis an enforceable standard.

**Key Activities:**

- NFR specification standard; universal-property/invariant verification standard; a test-type taxonomy standard that makes "declared" mean "operational and CI-invoked".

**Expected Outcomes:**

- Quality attributes and negatives become uniformly specified, verified requirements.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#phase-3-seams-and-supporting-axes]

#### Phase 3: Seams and supporting axes

**Strategic Objectives:**

- Make every seam class and the data model enforceable.

**Key Activities:**

- AsyncAPI event-contract standard (symmetric to the OpenAPI mandate); canonical-model standard; the design-first seam-contract pattern; application authorization policy-as-code guidance.

**Expected Outcomes:**

- Every cross-component edge and shared shape is an owned, verified artifact.
page_texts.23:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#phase-4-pattern-completion-and-socialization]

#### Phase 4: Pattern completion and socialization

**Strategic Objectives:**

- Complete reusable coverage and give the model a narrative home.

**Key Activities:**

- Foundation-before-fan-out sequencing pattern; property-based test specification pattern; journey-composition (Arazzo) pattern; this white paper.

**Expected Outcomes:**

- Every axis has both an enforceable standard and a reusable pattern; the model is teachable enterprise-wide.

page_texts.25:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#immediate-priorities]

### Immediate Priorities

1. **Ratify the operating model and elevate the core principles**

    - Advance ADR-GOV-011 through ARB, and have the principle owners ratify the Interface/Seam Accountability and Multi-Axis Decomposition principles.
    - Expected outcome: enforceable, discoverable doctrine.
    - Stakeholders: ARB, Governance/Application EA Leads.

2. **Adopt the per-axis standards as merge gates**

    - Wire the NFR, invariant, test-taxonomy, event-contract, and canonical-model standards into the architecture health check so each axis is a hard gate.
    - Expected outcome: "built by no one" failures become impossible to merge.
    - Stakeholders: Platform Engineering, Application/Information/Security EA Leads.
page_texts.26:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#medium-term-initiatives]

### Medium-term Initiatives

1. **Apply the model to a flagship agentic delivery**

    - Prove the end-to-end model on a real cross-context capability (e.g. enrollment), including a foundation, seams across contexts, invariants, and a journey.
    - Strategic value: evidence base and reference implementation for broad adoption.

2. **Instrument completeness reporting**

    - Report capability completeness by axis coverage, replacing behavior-only "% done".
    - Strategic value: leadership sees true readiness, not a proxy.
page_texts.27:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#long-term-strategic-direction]

### Long-term Strategic Direction

1. **Agentic delivery as the default**

    - With the model enforced, expand autonomous-agent delivery across the portfolio with confidence in integration correctness and compliance.

2. **Continuous conformance**

    - Extend from merge-time gates to continuous conformance (runtime invariant monitoring, drift detection) so shipped systems stay correct against their specs.

page_texts.29:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#61-strategic-imperative]

### 6.1 Strategic Imperative

**Why This Matters:**

- **Inaction cost** — scaling agentic delivery on a behavior-only decomposition scales the "built by no one" failure with it: more parallel agents, more unbuilt seams, more silent compliance gaps.
- **Opportunity** — a multi-axis, contract-first model turns agents from a risk into a force multiplier, because they build against complete specifications.
- **Alignment** — the model is the connective tissue between Gainwell's spec-driven SDLC bet and the enterprise's accountability and compliance obligations.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md#62-call-to-action]

### 6.2 Call to Action

**Recommended Next Steps:**

1. ARB ratifies ADR-GOV-011 and the two guiding-principle elevations.
2. Leadership endorses the per-axis standards as enforceable merge gates.
3. Platform Engineering pilots the full model on one flagship agentic capability.

**The Strategic Message**: When the builder is an autonomous agent, the specification is the product. Decompose for the agent — nodes *and* edges, every axis, foundations first — or the gaps you used to fill with conversation become the gaps that ship.

### Industry Standards and Frameworks

- **OpenAPI 3.1 / AsyncAPI 3.0 / Arazzo**: the recognized contract standards for the sync-api, event, and journey seam classes.

- **Property-based testing & architecture-fitness functions**: verification of universal/negative invariants.

## Strategy Summary (TL;DR)

**Strategic Challenge:** Behavior-only decomposition omits the edges, properties, and foundations that autonomous agents cannot infer — so agents ship them unbuilt.

**Proposed Approach:** Decompose every capability along all six axes (behavior, seam, negative property, NFR, data, journey), build foundations before fan-out, and make each axis accountable via a design-time contract → owned work item → merge gate, grounded in the enterprise taxonomy.

**Expected Benefits:**

- Integration correctness and compliance by construction
- Safe, real concurrency for parallel/agentic delivery
- Enforceable, discoverable enterprise doctrine (not one pipeline's tribal practice)

**Critical Success Factors:**

- ARB ratification of the operating-model ADR and core principles
- Per-axis standards wired as merge gates
- A flagship pilot proving the end-to-end model

**Recommended First Steps:**

1. Ratify ADR-GOV-011 and the two guiding-principle elevations.
2. Adopt the per-axis standards as enforceable gates.
3. Pilot the full model on one cross-context capability.

**Primary Audience:** Enterprise & solution architects, Platform Engineering leadership, and the Architecture Review Board.
